title: Complex numbers
learner: Returning learners who remember algebra and trigonometry but need a coherent picture of complex values, their arithmetic and geometric representations.
assumedKnowledge: F04 standard angles, radians, and trig signs

include: Polar coordinates, arguments, and Euler form
Polar operations, powers, and all roots
exclude: Complex analysis, analytic functions, contour integration or branch-cut theory
General polynomial root algorithms and arbitrary symbolic complex logarithms
AC circuit laws, phasor amplitude/RMS conventions, Fourier/Laplace transforms
Changing shared parsers to accept j, symbolic exponentials or general functions

conventions: Use i in answer fields; j in electrical writing names the same unit.
Use radians in Euler exponentials. Degree quantities are explicitly labeled.
Principal argument interval(-π,π]; zero argument undefined.
A principal square-root value and a complete root set are distinct requests.

routes.quick: Four diagnostic probes route to individual lessons. Use Quick recall, complete each independent checkpoint, then the four-part mixed recall.
routes.full: Recover rectangular arithmetic, then conjugation and division, then polar/Euler representations, and finally powers and roots. Predict before revealing each geometric activity; record reasoning in notes.

escalation.text: MTH215/F02 provide full algebra and quadratic support; the linked OpenStax and MIT sections provide deeper complex-number instruction. CEE300, CEE310 and CEE324 are course destinations for advanced applications beyond this refresher.

overlap: MTH215 m01-l03 and its F02 adapter already teach complex roots and exact multiplication/division.
F04 supplies exact standard-angle trig utilities and pi-multiple answers.
F07 supplies nonzero direction and magnitude conventions in the plane.
reuse.implementation: Wrap the committed mth-complex-arithmetic multiply/divide families under F09 identities with a version guard. Reuse parseExact, exact arithmetic, complex root-set grading, pi-multiple fields, and trigValue. Source lessons, saved attempts, storage and grading remain unchanged.

assessment.checkpoints: Four critical questions per lesson with multipart fields covering the entire objective and at most eight fields per question.
assessment.mixed: One multipart critical question per lesson objective; lesson checkpoints provide broader structural coverage.
assessment.evidence: Familiarity, visits, diagnostic, guided practice and interactive explorations remain separate from independent F09 lesson/mixed checkpoint evidence.

sharedCapabilities.integration: One strict union member and reader dispatch to scoped pure models and a keyboard-accessible component with equal-scale complex-plane diagrams and equivalent tables. No app-shell, parser or persistence redesign.

verification: Use100seeds per structure; independent Cartesian multiplication/division formulas, conjugate/norm identities, trigonometric reconstruction, repeated multiplication for powers and root verification.
Test exact equivalent complex/radical forms, complete unordered root sets, invalid i/j input guidance, zero divisor/base/argument cases and signed/axis quadrants.
Check every diagram's axis scales, zero points and root count; all lesson/example math and50seed practice/checkpoint generation.

Exercise all guided and activity modes, diagnostic routing, every independent checkpoint, mixed review, notes, resume and backup in desktop/mobile browsers; keyboard and Axe; run full tests/lint/type/build.
Label preview only after all verification; human review remains pending. Finish F09 before detailed F10 planning.
